JUDGMENT CALLS.
(a) Crossing at (293,428): verified at 12x -- the vertical carrying R4's bottom lead down to the ground rail makes a clear semicircular bulge to the right around the y~428 horizontal (the n11 wire running to the base of BJT 20). Unambiguous HOP, two separate nets. R4 bottom is on 0; the horizontal stays on n11.
(b) Crossing at (366,188): verified at 14x -- the vertical from Diode 10's cathode to Diode 13's anode makes a clear semicircular bulge to the right around the y~188 horizontal (the n9 / +5V rail). Unambiguous HOP. This leaves n13 (the diode-diode midpoint) a 2-terminal node reachable only through the two diodes -- electrically fine (it has a DC path via D10 to n12 and via D13 to n14), and it is what the ink shows.
(c) BJT arrow readings, all checked at 12-20x. The four PNPs 2, 3, 5, 21 and PNP 20 each show the emitter arrowhead with its V opening away from the lead's far end and its tip aimed at the base bar; the NPNs 1, 6, 7, 12 show the arrowhead aimed away from the base bar. Assigned emitters accordingly: BJT 3 emitter = upper lead (up at x~78), BJT 5 emitter = upper lead (up to 133,197), BJT 21 emitter = upper lead (up to the +6V node), BJT 2 emitter = upper lead (up to the +5V node), BJT 20 emitter = upper lead (up at x~372); BJT 1 emitter = lower-left lead to the ground rail, BJT 6 emitter = lower-right lead to the ground rail, BJT 7 emitter = lower-right lead to GND 9, BJT 12 emitter = lower-right lead to the +5V node. Every PNP emitter lands on the more positive node and every NPN emitter on the more negative one, so the arrow reading and the circuit sense agree.
(d) Terminal order is collector, base, emitter for all nine BJTs; anode-then-cathode for Diodes 10 and 13 (both drawn with the triangle above and the cathode bar below, so anode = top lead).
(e) Junction at (128,120) where the +70V stub (V-DC one-port 16) meets the R11/R18 column is a plain T, not a crossing -- the stub terminates there.
(f) All four V-DC (one port) symbols are bare arrow stubs (+3V, +6V, +70V, +5V) with a single lead; each is given the net of the wire it touches.
(g) No component is off-frame: R0 (centre x=9.9) and V-DC 14 (centre x=13.3) sit hard against the left edge but both symbols are fully visible and traceable.
(h) Resistor terminal order is top-then-bottom for the vertical resistors 0, 4, 11, 18 and left-then-right for the horizontal resistors 8 and 19.
